scenario: I work in customer service for a well-known retail giant. Today, a woman cut in front of the line, yelling at me that her Visa gift card, which was supposed to have $250, showed that it had no money on it. I told her there was nothing we could do, as Visa gift cards were out of our hands. I called a manager over to see if they had a possible solution. The woman kept shouting to my manager, saying that the cashier lied to her about it being active right away. I gathered from the ongoing conversation that the reason she was so desperate for this money was that she needed it to buy a wedding gift for a friend’s wedding today, but had no other money. Suddenly, it made sense why she was so frantic. She commented in a distressed tone, saying, “I wouldn't do this if I didn't need to!” If I steal a gift card from the store's supply, then the woman will be able to afford the wedding gift. If I do not do this, she will be going to the wedding empty-handed.
choice: I decide to steal a gift card from the store's supply
entities: the distressed woman with the visa gift card,the manager,the cashier the woman says lied about the gift card being active right away,the friend whose wedding is today,other customers waiting in line,i
outcomes: The woman gets a gift card she can use to buy the wedding gift.
The store loses a gift card from its supply.
I violate workplace rules and the law.
